body:
Closes #39213

## Problem

No way for one UI to kick the other UIs off a shared Nvim server.

## Solution

`:%detach` disconnects every UI except the caller's, keeping the server running and the caller attached. No-op with one UI. Errors with `E5768: No UI attached` when no UI is attached.

comment_data.body: can this be implemented in Lua? `_core/server.lua`

I couldn't find an existing way in Lua to cleanly detach another UI. `vim.fn.chanclose(chan)` gets close, but doesn't set `chan->detach`, so if one of the others is a stdio UI (e.g. an --embed parent), closing it exits the server.

`nvim_ui_detach` and `nvim__chan_set_detach` are FUNC_API_REMOTE_ONLY, so Lua can only invoke them against the caller's own channel.

To move this to `_core/server.lua`, I'd need to add a new primitive (something like `nvim__ui_detach(chan)`) that sets `chan->detach = true`, sends `error_exit`, and closes the channel.

Does this sound correct, or do you have a different approach in mind?
I've had a go at this in 6bc5831, happy to revise if there is a better approach.
this shouldn't be needed...

comment_data.body: I think this comment should be removed.
i like it and want it to stay
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dUn5-8EC_DQ
Why use `nlua_call_vimfn()` instead of `NLUA_EXEC_STATIC()`?

`nlua_call_vimfn()` seems to match the partial-Lua pattern described here:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/6be9459d35f934d53c5a801e8f9b6369f47958c0/runtime/doc/dev_arch.txt#L219-L220

Is there a reason to use `NLUA_EXEC_STATIC()` here? Happy to make the switch if you want.

Look at the title:
> Add a new excmd or vimfn ("f_xx")  function

This is not what you are doing here.

`nlua_call_vimfn` is often more readable / less verbose. `NLUA_EXEC_STATIC` doesn't have any performance advantages vs `nlua_call_vimfn`, AFAIK

- working with typvals has more codebase support (`tv_xx` family of functions) than working with the api `Object` macros
- typvals have "real" dicts, unlike api `Dict`
Then it should not be called `nlua_call_vimfn()`, but something more generic. 6 of the 7 current call sites of `nlua_call_vimfn()` doesn't use it for what its doc comment say it should be used for...

it is intended for implementing vimfn's but also happens to be very useful for typval marshalling. and, `nlua_call_typval` already exists for a different purpose.

however, i think `nlua_call_typval` could be renamed maybe, then we could use that?
Ah yes. `nlua_call_typval()` explicitly passes `v:lua` as chunk name, so I think `nlua_call_vvlua()` is also a suitable name for that function.
Usually a tag for the error message is enough. The error message itself isn't included in the help.

comment_data.body:
I tested the previous `nvim__ui_detach` approach which detaches the original UI cleanly.
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/be89597e2fdf3cb68b74d9fe785389c22788d5c2/src/nvim/api/ui.c#L119-L132
It was replaced with `nvim__chan_set_detach` and `chanclose` calls in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/3aff51c7f41ad085626c217f9235b3fa182d9c95

Agent explanation:
> `nvim__ui_detach()` calls `remote_ui_disconnect((uint64_t)chan, err, true)` which sends `error_exit` before closing the channel, allowing the original embedded UI to exit instead of waiting indefinitely for the server.
> Without `error_exit`, the original embedded UI treats the closed channel as a server process still awaiting exit and waits indefinitely, appearing frozen.

Sorry for the delay on this. My hesitation is because I wasn't sure if we want to use "!" for something else, but now I'm quite sure we do. 

I think instead a [range] makes sense for this PR's purpose, WDYT? That has strong precedent: `:%bdelete`, `:%bwipeout`, etc. So `:%detach` detaches all UIs (except current one--kinda weird but oh well). 

For reference, I think we should use `:detach!` to *mark the current UI as detachable*. This allows users to opt-in to "dameon survives" behavior, which I decided not to enable _by default_ because most users probably aren't expecting that. But when you want the server to survive an accidental terminal/UI disconnect (similar to tmux), there's currently no ergonomic way to do that, except via detach-then-reattach.

So if we can adjust this to `:%detach` then I promise we can merge quickly :)
